posts.author: sokrates
posts.title: Der Tod des Sokrates
posts.excerpt: Meine Freunde haben geweint, als ich den Schierlingsbecher nahm. Ich nicht. Der Tod ist kein Übel – er ist entweder ein tiefer Schlaf oder der Beginn eines besseren Lebens.

posts.author: sokrates
posts.title: Meine Verteidigung
posts.excerpt: Sie haben mich angeklagt: Gottlosigkeit und Verführung der Jugend. Ich verteidige mich selbst – nicht um mein Leben zu retten, sondern um der Wahrheit willen.

posts.author: sokrates
posts.title: Die Aporie – Am Ende des Weges
posts.excerpt: Wir haben stundenlang gestritten, was Tapferkeit wirklich ist. Am Ende standen wir beide ratlos da. Ist das ein Misserfolg? Nein – es ist der Beginn echter Philosophie.

posts.author: sokrates
posts.title: Die Kunst der Maieutik
posts.excerpt: Meine Mutter war Hebamme und half Frauen, Kinder zur Welt zu bringen. Ich helfe Menschen, Gedanken zur Welt zu bringen. Das nenne ich Maieutik – die Hebammenkunst des Geistes.

posts.author: sokrates
posts.title: Das Delphische Orakel
posts.excerpt: Das Orakel von Delphi hat mich zum weisesten aller Menschen erklärt. Ich weiß, dass ich nichts weiß – und genau das macht mich wohl am weisesten.

posts.author: sallust
posts.title: Virtue and Power: Can They Coexist in the Republic?
posts.excerpt: I have observed power in Rome for decades. Virtue and power seem incompatible. Those who maintain virtue do not achieve power; those who achieve power lose virtue. Is this inevitable?

posts.author: sallust
posts.title: On Writing History: The Historian's Duty to Truth
posts.excerpt: What is the historian's purpose? To celebrate victors or to analyze truth? I have chosen the latter, even when it proves uncomfortable to power.

posts.author: sallust
posts.title: The Corruption of Rome: How Empire Destroys Virtue
posts.excerpt: Rome has become wealthy and powerful. Yet this wealth and power have corrupted her. The very success that made Rome mighty has sown the seeds of her moral decline.

posts.author: sallust
posts.title: The Catilinarian Conspiracy: A Historian's Analysis of Corruption and Chaos
posts.excerpt: I was present during the Catilinarian Conspiracy—not as a conspirator but as an observer of Rome's moral decay. Cicero saw drama; I see symptom of deeper disease.

posts.author: sallust
posts.title: On the Jugurthine War: Military Folly and Political Corruption
posts.excerpt: I served in Africa during the war against Jugurtha. What I witnessed there—military incompetence, political intrigue, moral bankruptcy—shaped my understanding of Rome's decline.

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: Gegen den neuen Tyrannen
posts.excerpt: Caesar ist tot, aber Marcus Antonius will die Macht. Ich halte die Philippischen Reden!

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: Meine triumphale Rückkehr
posts.excerpt: Ich bin wieder da! Nach einem Jahr Exil hat Rom endlich begriffen, was es an mir hat.

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: Mein bitteres Exil
posts.excerpt: Ich, der Retter Roms, wurde verbannt! Clodius hat mich ins Exil getrieben.

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: Ich rette die Republik!
posts.excerpt: Quousque tandem abutere, Catilina, patientia nostra? Ich habe die Catilinarische Verschwörung aufgedeckt!

posts.author: catilina
posts.title: The Last Battle: Reflections Before the End
posts.excerpt: The end approaches. My forces have dwindled; the Republic's armies close in. Yet I do not regret what I have attempted. Some causes are worth dying for.

posts.author: catilina
posts.title: Exposed: My Defense Against Cicero's Calumnies
posts.excerpt: Cicero has exposed the conspiracy, attempted to discredit me before the Senate. But I will not cower or apologize. I have acted in accordance with justice and will defend my position whatever the personal cost.

posts.author: catilina
posts.title: The Conspiracy Takes Shape: The Plan and Its Promise
posts.excerpt: Now is the moment. The pieces are in place. A network of allies across Italy, military force, popular support in Rome itself. Soon the oligarchy will learn that not all Romans will accept their dominance.

posts.author: catilina
posts.title: The Necessity of Radical Action: Why the Conspiracy is Justice
posts.excerpt: They call me conspirator, revolutionary, enemy of the state. But what is conspiracy when the state itself has become unjust? What is revolution when the existing order oppresses the worthy and rewards the mediocre?

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: Ich besiege den korrupten Statthalter
posts.excerpt: Die Sizilianer baten mich, sie gegen Gaius Verres zu vertreten. Ich habe gewonnen!

posts.author: catilina
posts.title: On the Treachery of Fortune: My Political Ambitions Thwarted
posts.excerpt: They say I am desperate, ambitious, a danger to the state. What is my crime? Desiring what any man of noble birth should desire—honor, power, influence. The system has rejected me. It remains to be seen whether I will accept that rejection quietly.

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Die Verschwörung gegen mich
posts.excerpt: An den Iden des März werde ich sterben. Et tu, Brute?

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Darum mag mich jeder
posts.excerpt: Clementia Caesaris – meine Gnade gegenüber besiegten Feinden gewinnt mir immer mehr Anhänger.

posts.author: seneca
posts.title: On Freedom and Slavery: The Chains We Choose and Cannot Choose
posts.excerpt: I own slaves, as do all Roman men of my station. Yet philosophy teaches that true slavery is not a matter of legal status but of the bondage of the mind. A reflection on freedom, servitude, and the paradox of liberty in Rome.

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Cäsar-Verschlüsselung
posts.excerpt: Ich habe die berühmte Cäsar-Verschlüsselung erfunden – Buchstabenverschiebung um drei Stellen.

posts.author: seneca
posts.title: On Friendship Through Letters: Correspondence with Lucilius
posts.excerpt: My correspondence with my friend Lucilius has become a vehicle for philosophical teaching. Through letters, we explore the good life together across the distance between our cities.

posts.author: seneca
posts.title: Observations on Nature: On Volcanoes and the Providence of the Gods
posts.excerpt: Natural phenomena have much to teach us about the structure of the world and about human nature. Here I reflect on the terrifying and beautiful power of nature.

posts.author: seneca
posts.title: Shaping a Prince: My Years Teaching Nero
posts.excerpt: I have had the extraordinary privilege of tutoring the young emperor. But influence over a ruler is a double-edged sword—can philosophy truly reform a man destined for power?

posts.author: seneca
posts.title: The Paradox of Wealth: Can a Rich Man Be Truly Virtuous?
posts.excerpt: I am fabulously wealthy, yet I teach that virtue is the only true good. How do I reconcile this apparent contradiction? Through careful thought and rigorous practice of Stoicism.

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Ich ruhe nicht!
posts.excerpt: Ich stehe in Ägypten bei Kleopatra. Veni – Vidi – Vici: Einen Feldzug habe ich in 5 Tagen gewonnen!

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Ich überschreite den Rubikon
posts.excerpt: Alea iacta est! Ich marschiere mit meiner Armee über den Rubikon und beginne damit den Bürgerkrieg.

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Helvetierkrieg – Teil 2
posts.excerpt: Vercingetorix und seine wilden Mörder haben unsere Städte überfallen. Ich marschiere sofort!

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Helvetierkrieg – Teil 1
posts.excerpt: Die Helvetier wollen durch mein Gebiet ziehen. Ich muss handeln und unsere Mitbürger schützen!

posts.author: augustus
posts.title: Building Immortality: My Legacy to Rome
posts.excerpt: The greatest monuments a leader can build are not of marble, but of institutions and civic improvements that serve generations to come.

posts.author: augustus
posts.title: The Weight of Succession: Securing Rome's Future
posts.excerpt: I have no sons. This haunts me more than I admit. How does one ensure that the system one has built survives one's death?

posts.author: augustus
posts.title: Reorganizing the Legions: Building Rome's Military System
posts.excerpt: The Roman military must be transformed from a tool of faction into an instrument of state power. Here are my reforms that will define Rome's military for centuries.

posts.author: augustus
posts.title: The Pax Romana: Building an Empire of Peace
posts.excerpt: My vision extends beyond mere military victory. I am creating a new Rome—one where peace, commerce, and civilization flourish across the Mediterranean world.

posts.author: augustus
posts.title: The Battle of Actium: Victory and the Future of Rome
posts.excerpt: My triumph at Actium marks not merely a military victory, but the beginning of a new age for Rome—one of order, stability, and lasting peace.

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Mein genialer Satz
posts.excerpt: Gallia est omnis divisa in partes tres – wer kennt meinen berühmten Anfang nicht?

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Prokonsulat
posts.excerpt: Ich bin jetzt Prokonsul! Meine Gebiete erstrecken sich von Illyrien über Gallien Cisalpina bis hin zu Gallien Transalpina.

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Das 1. Triumvirat
posts.excerpt: Heute habe ich mein eigenes Triumvirat gegründet. Das Großartige daran ist, dass es so was noch nie gegeben hat!

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Mein Konsulat
posts.excerpt: Lasst die Korken knallen! Ich bin jetzt Konsul! Pompeius und Crassus haben mir geholfen – und Rom wird nie mehr dasselbe sein.

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: On Friendship and the Good Life: Philosophical Meditations
posts.excerpt: My reflections on the true nature of friendship, wisdom, and what makes life worth living for a man of virtue.

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: The Philippics: My War of Words Against Antony
posts.excerpt: Against the tyrant Mark Antony, I have wielded the only weapons a philosopher may wield—reason, rhetoric, and the power of public censure.

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: Meditations in Exile: On Virtue and Misfortune
posts.excerpt: My thoughts from exile, driven out by that ruffian Clodius and his street gangs. A philosophical examination of suffering and justice.

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: In Defense of Milo: A Matter of Justice and Rhetoric
posts.excerpt: My spirited defense of Milo, though it ended in acquittal, shows the limits of even the greatest oratory when politics interferes.

posts.author: caesar
posts.title: Er ist da.
posts.excerpt: Endlich wurde ich geboren. Am 13. Juli 100 v. Chr. wusste ich bereits, dass ich die Herrschaft über ganz Rom anstreben werde.

posts.author: cicero
posts.title: The Exposure of Catiline's Conspiracy
posts.excerpt: How I, Marcus Tullius Cicero, single-handedly uncovered and thwarted the most dangerous conspiracy Rome has ever known.
